# Summary and Questions

**Paper:** Bernien et al., "Probing many-body dynamics on a 51-atom quantum simulator," *Nature* **551**, 579–584 (2017) [@bernien2017probing]

**Architecture:** 1-zone analog (Harvard lab)

## What was done

The first large-scale Rydberg tweezer array experiment: 51 $^{87}$Rb atoms in a 1D chain with van der Waals interactions in the Rydberg blockade regime. The experiment performed:

1. **Adiabatic state preparation:** Slow detuning sweeps from $\Delta < 0$ (paramagnetic) to $\Delta > 0$ (ordered), preparing crystalline $\mathbb{Z}_2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_3$ ordered states with high fidelity.
2. **Quench dynamics:** Sudden quench from the disordered phase deep into the ordered regime, monitoring the subsequent real-time evolution of the many-body state.
3. **Single-shot fluorescence imaging:** Measuring the Rydberg excitation pattern of all 51 atoms after each experimental shot.

## Key observations

- **Phase transitions into ordered states:** Observed $\mathbb{Z}_2$ (every other atom excited), $\mathbb{Z}_3$ (every third atom), and $\mathbb{Z}_4$ (every fourth atom) crystalline orders as a function of blockade radius $R_b/a$, where $a$ is the lattice spacing. The Z₄ phase used a lattice spacing $a = 2.87\ \mu\text{m}$ with NN interaction $V_{i,i+1}/2\pi = 1536$ MHz — demonstrating the platform's programmability across multiple commensurate orders.
- **Persistent many-body oscillations:** After preparing the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ ordered state (via adiabatic sweep to large $\Delta > 0$) and then suddenly quenching to $\Delta = 0$ (the disordered/critical regime), the domain-wall density exhibited long-lived oscillations — persisting for $>4$ Rabi cycles — rather than thermalizing as expected from the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH).
- **Quantum many-body scars:** The oscillations were later identified [@turner2018quantum] as arising from a tower of special eigenstates (quantum many-body scars) embedded in an otherwise thermal spectrum, representing a novel mechanism of weak ergodicity breaking.

## Scientific significance

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|-----------|
| **Novelty** | First demonstration of a programmable Rydberg tweezer array as a many-body quantum simulator; discovery of quantum many-body scars as a new dynamical phenomenon. |
| **Practical value** | Established the experimental platform that all subsequent Lukin group work builds upon. No direct application, but the scar phenomenon has implications for quantum state preparation and information storage in non-equilibrium systems. |
| **Verification value** | First experimental observation of weak ergodicity breaking in a clean, isolated quantum system — previously only theorized in the context of single-particle quantum chaos. |


## Architecture comparison: relative to 1-zone/3-zone/4-zone review benchmarks

| Parameter | Bernien 2017 | SOTA 1-zone (Manovitz 2025) | Notes |
|-----------|-------------|---------------------------|-------|
| Atom count | 51 (1D) | ~300 (2D) | 6× fewer atoms, 1D only |
| Trap technology | 1D standing-wave (no SLM) | SLM + AOD | SLM introduced in Ebadi 2021 for 2D geometry |
| Loading probability | ~60% (no AOD rearrangement) | 98.4(7)% after rearrangement | Post-selected on filled configurations; no real-time rearrangement |
| Rydberg state | $\|70S_{1/2}\rangle$ | $\|70S_{1/2}\rangle$ | Same Rydberg level |
| Lattice spacing (Z₂) | $a = 5.74\ \mu\text{m}$, $R_b/a \approx 1.57$ | $a = 6.45$, $6.8$, $7.15\ \mu\text{m}$ (tuneable) | Blockade radius $R_b \approx 9\ \mu\text{m}$ |
| Quench Rabi freq. | $\Omega/2\pi = 2$ MHz | $\Omega/2\pi = 3.1\text{–}6.0$ MHz (varies by lattice spacing) | 1.5–3× lower depending on configuration |
| NN interaction | $V_{i,i+1}/2\pi = 24$ MHz | $V_{i,i+1}/2\pi \approx 12$ MHz (at $a = 6.45\ \mu\text{m}$, from $C_6/a^6$) | $V_{i,i+2}/2\pi = 0.38$ MHz (NNN) |
| Coherence (spin echo) | $> 5\ \mu\text{s}$ (no visible decay) | Improved PDH; ms-scale | 420 nm laser PDH-locked to finesse ≥4000 cavity |
| Readout fidelity | $\|g\rangle$ 98% (7-atom) / 99% (51-atom), $\|r\rangle$ 93% | $\|g\rangle$ ~99%, $\|r\rangle$ ~92–96% | No significant degradation in later systems |
| Atom temperature | ~12 μK in ~1 mK trap | — | Rydberg lifetime $\approx 150\ \mu\text{s}$ (70S, 300 K) |

This experiment predates the SLM+AOD architecture (introduced in Ebadi 2021). The jump from 1D standing-wave traps to 2D SLM-generated arrays is the most significant hardware difference.


## Critical technique analysis

**Most important bottleneck for this specific experiment: Decoherence truncates the scar oscillations.**

The domain-wall density oscillations in Fig. 3 of the paper decay with an estimated $1/e$ timescale of **~0.88 μs** (estimated from digitized Fig. 3 data; the paper does not report a decay constant explicitly) — roughly 1–2 Rabi periods at $\Omega/2\pi = 2$ MHz. The oscillations are visible for only ~4 cycles before being washed out. The spin-echo coherence is $> 5\ \mu\text{s}$ (no visible decay), so simple dephasing is not the dominant mechanism. The competing decoherence channels are:

- **Intermediate-state scattering (dominant channel):** The two-photon Rydberg excitation via $6P_{3/2}$ has an off-resonant scattering rate of $0.022\ \mu\text{s}^{-1}$ per atom ($\approx 2\pi \times 3.5$ kHz; Methods of [@bernien2017probing]). For 51 atoms this gives a collective scattering rate of $51 \times 0.022\ \mu\text{s}^{-1} \approx 1.12\ \mu\text{s}^{-1}$, corresponding to a $1/e$ time of $\sim 0.89\ \mu\text{s}$ — consistent with the observed 0.88 μs oscillation decay timescale. This is the dominant decoherence channel during driven evolution.
- **Rydberg state decay:** Lifetime $\tau \approx 150\ \mu\text{s}$ for $|70S_{1/2}\rangle$ at 300 K, contributing a decay rate of $\sim 2\pi \times 1$ kHz per atom. For 51 atoms this gives a collective $1/e$ time $\sim 3\ \mu\text{s}$ — a secondary contribution, $\sim 3\times$ slower than intermediate-state scattering.
- **Thermal motion dephasing:** Atom temperature ~12 μK in a ~1 mK trap gives a root-mean-square position spread that modulates the van der Waals coupling $V \propto r^{-6}$, smearing the blockade edge.
- **Laser phase noise:** The 420 nm excitation laser is PDH-locked (finesse ≥4000), but residual phase noise at MHz frequencies directly dephases the driven Rabi oscillations.

**Why improving coherence would help:** Longer coherence would allow the experiment to observe more oscillation cycles, unambiguously distinguishing true many-body scars (non-decaying oscillations in the thermodynamic limit) from finite-size effects or prethermal plateaus. The 4-cycle observation window in Bernien 2017 was sufficient to motivate the scar interpretation [@turner2018quantum] but not to rule out alternatives. The subsequent theoretical and experimental literature largely focused on this ambiguity.

:::{.callout-note icon="false"}
## Experiment Protocol

1. **Load:** 51 $^{87}$Rb atoms into a 1D optical tweezer chain (spacing $a = 5.74\ \mu\text{m}$ for Z₂ experiments); post-select on filled configurations (~60% per-site loading probability, no real-time rearrangement).
2. **Prepare:** Adiabatically sweep detuning from $\Delta_{\min} < 0$ (paramagnetic) through resonance to $\Delta_{\max} > 0$ (Z₂/Z₃ ordered phase) while simultaneously ramping $\Omega$. The detuning ramp uses optimized functional forms: a **tangent** sweep $V(t) = a\tan[b(t - t_0)] + c$ for the 51-atom datasets (better performance), or a **cubic** sweep $V(t) = a(t - t_0)^3 + b(t - t_0) + c$ for smaller system sizes and the crystal dynamics data. All sweep parameters ($a, b, c, t_0$, sweep bounds $\Delta_{\min}$, $\Delta_{\max}$) are iteratively optimized to minimize the domain-wall number. For 51 atoms, the perfect $\mathbb{Z}_2$ state is obtained with probability $P = 0.11(2)\%$ raw ($0.9(2)\%$ corrected for detection fidelity), with an average of 9.01(2) domain walls (5.4 after maximum-likelihood correction). For a 7-atom cluster, fidelity reaches 54(4)% raw (77(6)% corrected).
3. **Quench (for scar experiments):** From the adiabatically prepared $\mathbb{Z}_2$ state (at large $\Delta > 0$), suddenly set $\Delta = 0$ at $t = 0$ with $\Omega = 2\pi \times 2$ MHz, evolving in the disordered/critical regime.
4. **Evolve:** Hold for variable post-quench time $t \in [0,\ 1.2\text{–}1.5\ \mu\text{s}]$ (the total experimental window including the adiabatic ramp is ~3 μs; the quench evolution window shown in Fig. 3 is ~1.2–1.5 μs).
5. **Measure:** Turn off all fields; image atoms via single-photon fluorescence. Repeat ~1,000 realizations per time point for domain-wall density measurements; the Z₂ probability distribution figure (Fig. 5c) used **18,439 realizations**.
:::


## Key Hamiltonian parameters

The experiment realizes the PXP-like Hamiltonian in the blockade approximation:

$$H = \sum_i \frac{\Omega}{2} \sigma_i^x - \Delta n_i + \sum_{i<j} V_{ij} n_i n_j$$

with $n_i = \frac{1}{2}(1 + \sigma_i^z)$. Relevant parameters from the paper:

| Quantity | Value |
|---------|-------|
| Quench point | $\Delta = 0$, $\Omega = 2\pi \times 2$ MHz |
| 1013 nm single-photon Rabi freq. | $\Omega_R = 2\pi \times 36$ MHz (Methods) |
| 420 nm single-photon Rabi freq. | $\Omega_B = 2\pi \times 60$ MHz (Methods) |
| Intermediate-state detuning | $\delta = 2\pi \times 560$ MHz from $6P_{3/2}$ (Methods) |
| Lattice spacing (Z₂) | $a = 5.74\ \mu\text{m}$ |
| Lattice spacing (Z₃) | $a = 3.57\ \mu\text{m}$ |
| Lattice spacing (Z₄) | $a = 2.87\ \mu\text{m}$ |
| NN interaction (Z₄) | $V_{i,i+1}/2\pi = 1536$ MHz |
| Blockade radius | $R_b \approx 9\ \mu\text{m}$ ($R_b/a \approx 1.57$ for Z₂) |
| NN interaction $V_{i,i+1}$ | $2\pi \times 24$ MHz |
| NNN interaction $V_{i,i+2}$ | $2\pi \times 0.38$ MHz |
| Domain-wall oscillation period | ~0.69 μs (frequency $\approx \Omega/1.38$; with $\Omega/2\pi = 2$ MHz this gives $T = 1.38/(\Omega/2\pi) = 0.69\ \mu\text{s}$) |
| Domain-wall oscillation decay | ~0.88 μs (estimated from digitized Fig. 3; not explicitly reported in paper) |
| Intermediate-state scattering | $0.022\ \mu\text{s}^{-1}$ per atom ($\approx 2\pi \times 3.5$ kHz; Methods) |
| Rydberg lifetime (70S, 300 K) | ~150 μs |
| Atom temperature | ~12 μK |
| Trap depth | ~1 mK |
| Coherence (spin echo) | $> 5\ \mu\text{s}$ (no visible decay) |
| Z₂ preparation fidelity (51 atoms) | $P = 0.11(2)\%$ raw; $0.9(2)\%$ detection-corrected; 9.01(2) domain walls raw, ~5.4 corrected |
| Z₂ preparation fidelity (7 atoms) | 54(4)% raw; 77(6)% detection-corrected |
| Shots per time point | ~1,000 realizations |
| Rabi frequency inhomogeneity | $< 3\%$ peak-to-peak (controlled tolerance across chain) |
| Rydberg laser linewidth (PDH) | $< 0.5$ kHz |
| Experimental cycle time | ~250 ms |
| Trap-off duration (for Rydberg) | $\leq 7\ \mu\text{s}$ (capped at 3% atom loss) |
